title: schema-aware response mode with soft-strict backoff and OpenAI-compat mapping
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: users building structured output integrations require stronger guarantees that models produce JSON that conforms to a declared schema, but strict enforcement can break streaming UX and tool/function calling semantics. This PR introduces a runtime `schema_mode` set of behaviors (default: 'soft-strict') that attempts strict validation where possible but automatically falls back to a permissive compatibility path during streaming or tool calls to preserve liveness.

What this PR implements: 1) new API parameter mapping: maps OpenAI-style response_format/schema hints into Redwood's `schema_mode` + `response_format` conventions (OpenAI: 'json_schema' -> Redwood: schema_mode='soft-strict', response_format='json'). 2) Soft-strict backoff: during streaming, the validator runs incrementally and will: (a) accept well-formed chunks and emit inline diagnostics to token metadata, (b) on detection of irrecoverable schema violation mid-stream, emit a stream checkpoint token with a rewind hint and switch to permissive compatibility mode for remaining tokens, attaching a structured error payload in final response metadata. 3) Tool/function-call safepoints: when tool calls are involved, the runtime will enforce stricter output contracts before invoking tools; if strict enforcement would block tool invocation (model not yet conforming), runtime will attempt a lightweight coercion pass (type casts, minor key renames guided by schema aliases) and only if coercion fails will it record a tool-call abort event and continue in compat mode. 4) Improved error messaging: user-facing error codes (RFC-style short codes) and machine-readable diagnostics are attached to the final response metadata and available via the Console telemetry. 5) Backwards-compatible OpenAI bridge: the OpenAI compatibility layer receives the above behaviors mapped to legacy fields and a set of heuristics so existing clients see stable responses and informative warnings rather than hard failures.

Checklist: - [x] API mapping and request parsing - [x] Incremental streaming validator with checkpoint token - [x] Soft coercion utilities and schema alias rules - [x] Toolcall safepoint logic and abort/error signals - [x] Console telemetry hooks and nightingale metrics - [x] Unit + integration tests covering streaming violations, coercion, and toolcall interactions - [x] Docs update stub (docs/structured-output.md)

Rollout plan: feature-flagged on canary -> 25% host traffic for 48h -> 100% in two weeks. Breaking-change risk: low; default preserves old behavior for requests that don't opt into schema-aware response modes. See release_notes below for para guidance for customers.

review_conversation: Carlos Nguyen: Nice direction. A couple of questions: how do we ensure we don't regress latency for short responses? Suggest adding a fast-path for <128 tokens where we run a lenient post-hoc validator instead of incremental checks.
Aisha Patel: Added a fast-path in validator.ts and included benchmarks; short responses skip incremental checks unless client requests strict mode explicitly.
Sofie Larsson: Toolcall safepoint seems complex; can we decouple abort telemetry from user error? We shouldn't surface internal aborts as user facing 5xx.
Aisha Patel: Good catch — updated safepoint to emit user-facing errors with 'RWD-TOOL-ABORT' only when a tool would have been invoked. Internal aborts now emit internal-only telemetry tags.

Ethan Brooks: test matrix looks solid. One nit: rename schema_mode value 'strict-if-possible' -> 'strict-if-possible' is fine but document fallback precedence. Marked approved after small test rename.
Carlos Nguyen: Approved after CI green and test flake investigation.

release_notes: Introduces a schema-aware response mode (schema_mode) that improves structured-output stability. Default behavior remains backward-compatible; opt-in via schema_mode or OpenAI-style response hints to get stronger validation and diagnostics. Streaming responses now include checkpoint tokens and final metadata with machine-readable diagnostics when schema issues occur. See docs/structured-output.md for migration notes.
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind feature flag 'schema.soft_strict_backoff'. Canary traffic will be enabled for dedicated + hosted regions as described in rollout. Watch metrics: structured_output.validation_failure_rate, streaming.checkpoint_rate, toolcall.abort_rate.
user_facing_examples: Behavior: incremental diagnostics emitted on token stream, final response metadata includes errors if any coercion/backoff occured
